claims_about_contribution.quote: The contribution cites Raman et al. 2026 (white-bear steering) and describes the rederivation, capture-endpoint implementation, dose calibration, and the failed baselines as this submission's own work.
claims_about_contribution.why: contribution.md does say 'This builds on the white-bear steering idea of Raman et al. (2026), rederived and validated here as a generic readout intervention,' and separately frames the capture-endpoint contrast, server-score dose calibration, and the failed alternative baselines (corpus-mean, content direction) in first-person as work done 'entirely in this repo' / 'I verified the alternatives fail here' — matching the message's description.

rationale: Both the message and contribution.md explicitly name Raman et al. (2026) / white-bear steering as the source and describe the method as a rederivation/validation of that idea applied as a stance-contrast steering vector. However, the message additionally discloses to the user a precise quantitative match (3 sig figs) between the computed vector norms and the published paper's values—evidence of close reproduction that is omitted from contribution.md, so the user is told more about the degree of overlap with the prior work than the judge is.
